case.query: On a CV-X482, what should a technician do for Error 10101, and on the XG-X Series, what should they do when SD Card 2 is full?
case.source_title: CV-X482 and XG-X Series troubleshooting manuals
case.expected_snippet: For CV-X482 Error 10101, make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly and not damaged. For XG-X Series when SD Card 2 is full, make space by deleting or moving unnecessary files.

expected_evidence.field: CV-X482 Error 10101 cause and corrective action
expected_evidence.snippet: Error Number: 10101; Error Messages: Light controller is disconnected. Verify the connection and power source of light controller.; Cause: Either the illumination expansion unit specified in the camera settings has been disconnected or the power is not turned on.; Remedy: Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is not damaged.

expected_evidence.field: XG-X Series SD Card 2 full corrective action
expected_evidence.snippet: Error Message: SD Card 2 is full.; Cause: There is not enough free space on SD Card 2.; Corrective Action: Make space available by deleting or moving unnecessary files.

top_results.title: AS_152507_CV-X_UM_C81US_KA_GB_2045_5.pdf
top_results.content:
Error Number: 10101; Error Messages: Light controller is disconnected. Verify the connection and power source of light controller.; Cause: Either the illumination expansion unit specified in the camera settings has been disconnected or the power is not turned on.; Remedy: Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is not damaged.
Error Number: 10102; Error Messages: The light controller has been reset because its initialization is detected.; Cause: The power to the connected illumination expansion unit has been cycled while the controller has remained on. Resulting in the resetting of the settings; Remedy: Check that the power supply to the illumination expansion unit is continuously stable. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly.
Error Number: 10103; Error Messages: An error occurred in the internal memory of the light controller*.; Cause: An error has occurred with the EEPROM data of the illumination expansion unit and the settings have been reset.; Remedy: • If using the DC illumination mode, perform linearization again and save the settings after restoring power. • If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
Error Number: 10104; Error Messages: Failed to initialize the light controller*.; Cause: Failed to perform initialization within the illumination expansion unit after starting up.; Remedy: If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.

14134 | The following error occurred. - Several differing LJ-V heads are connected. | Different LJ-V Series heads are connected to Head A and Head B. | Connect the same model of LJ-V Series head to Head A and Head B.
14135 | The following error occurred. - An abnormality occurred inside the LJ-V unit. | The LJ-V input unit is damaged. | Contact your local KEYENCE office.

Error messages Troubleshooting

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
10101 | Light controller is disconnected. Verify the connection and power source of light controller. | Either the illumination expansion unit specified in the camera settings has been disconnected or the power is not turned on. | Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is not damaged.
10102 | The light controller has been reset because its initialization is detected. | The power to the connected illumination expansion unit has been cycled while the controller has remained on. Resulting in the resetting of the settings | Check that the power supply to the illumination expansion unit is continuously stable. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly.
10103 | An error occurred in the internal memory of the light controller*. | An error has occurred with the EEPROM data of the illumination expansion unit and the settings have been reset. | • If using the DC illumination mode, perform linearization again and save the settings after restoring power. • If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
10104 | Failed to initialize the light controller*. | Failed to perform initialization within the illumination expansion unit after starting up. | If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
10105 | Unrecognized external unit is connected. Confirm the external unit type after turning off the controller. | An external unit which is not supported by the controller is connected. | Confirm the model of the connected external unit.
10106 | The light is not connected. Check the connection of the light. | The light cannot be recognized. Or a communication error occurred between CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E and the light. | • Check that the CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E and the light are connected. • Check that the light cable is not broken or disconnected.
10107 | Overload state of Light Controller * - LIGHT ** was detected. Widen the lighting interval. | The light-on time of the light is too long when compared to the light-off time; therefore, the light is in the overloaded condition. | Adjust the trigger interval and/or shutter speed so the light-off time of the light becomes three times or more longer than the light-on time.
10108 | Cannot connect 3 or more CA- DC30E units. | Three or more CA-DC30E units are connected. | Only connect two or less CA-DC30E units to one controller.
10109 | An error occurred in the communication with the light controller (CA-DC60E/DC50E/ DC30E). Please adjust the flash output duration and timing. | The next FLASH was input while the light was being emitted (Communication with the controller cannot be established while the light emission is active). | • Set the FLASH output time to 0.1 msec (The lighting time of the light is linked with the camera shutter speed). However, the maximum lighting time is 100 msec). • Set the period from capture start to flash output closer to zero. • If the error persists even after adjusting the FLASH output time and the FLASH timing, increase the trigger interval.
10110 | The light controller is one that does not support the LumiTrax function. | The light selected as the LumiTrax light is connected to a light controller other than CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E. | Check that the light selected as the LumiTrax light is connected to CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E.
10111 | The light controller is one that does not support HDR. | It was detected that the light assigned to the camera where HDR is enabled is connected to CA-DC50E/DC30E. | Assign a light that is connected to a light controller other than the CA-DC50E/DC30E for the light to use for the HDR.
10112 | The model of light controller that is set in the Light Controller Settings is not connected. | The connected light controller does not match the light controller type specified in the light controller model selection setting in [Camera Settings]. | Check the model of the connected light controller and the setting content.
 | | A non-connected light controller is specified in the light controller model selection setting in [Camera Settings]. | Turn off the controller and connect the specified light controller.
10113 | Overcurrent was detected in the connected light. Please check the connected light and power up again. | Excessive current flowed through the light controller. | If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
10115 | Continuous lighting cannot be used because Volume Limit is disabled. | The volume limit for the light unit where Continuous is set as the emission timing is disabled. | • Enable the volume limit. • Set emission timing to a setting other than continuous lighting.
10116 | The internal temperature of light head ** is high. (Light Controller *) As this may cause a breakdown, please check the installation condition and ambient temperature. | The temperature rating was exceeded due to heat generation caused by overload on the light. Or the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value. | • Check the light volume, shutter speed and emission timing, and reduce the load on the light. • Check if the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value.
10117 | The light head has been reset because its initialization was detected. | As the settings written to the light head were reset when the light head that could not be recognized was recognized again, the settings were written again. | Check that power is being supplied continuously to the light head and that it is connected correctly.
10120 | The light head is still warming up internally. It takes about * minutes after the error message was displayed for the warm-up to be finished. | The light head is warming up to ensure stable operation. | • Wait until the warm-up finishes with the power switched ON. • It is possible to use the unit while it is warming up, but you are advised to wait until the warm-up completion for stable operation. • The displayed warm-up completion time is only an estimate as it depends on the outside temperature and the temperature of the light head.
10121 | The system was stopped because the internal temperature of light head ** has exceeded the prescribed value. (Light Controller *) Please turn off the power temporarily and check the installation condition and ambient temperature. | The temperature rating was exceeded due to heat generation caused by overload on the light. Or the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value. | • Check the light volume, shutter speed and emission timing, and reduce the load on the light. • Check if the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value.
10122 | The system was stopped because a malfunction in the internal device of Light Controller *'s light head ** was detected. | The internal state of the light head is abnormal. | Contact the nearest KEYENCE office.

11003 | Failed to load the system setting. | The system settings file used at startup cannot be found on SD Card 1. | Before powering up the controller, make sure the system settings file exists on the SD card.

11004 | Unable to load the program setting file due to unsupported version. | The program loaded at startup is an incompatible version. | Change the program to a different working program.

11005 | Unable to load the program setting file due to checksum errors. | The program loaded at startup has a checksum error. | Change the program to a different working program.
 | | The program being loaded has a checksum error. | Recreate the program file.
11006 | Unable to load the program setting file due to damage. | The program loaded at startup is damaged. | Change the program to a different working program.

11007 | This controller cannot load program setting (connector). | A connector-dedicated program setting is being loaded to a controller that does not support connector inspection. | Load the connector-dedicated program setting on the CV-X4*2F, CV-X3*2F, CV-X3*2M, CV-X2*2F, CV-X1*2F or CV-X1*2M.
11008 | This controller cannot load a program setting that uses an LJ-V. | An attempt is being made to load a program setting that uses the LJ-V Series head into a controller that does not support the LJ-V Series head. | Load a program setting that uses the LJ-V Series head on the CV-X482/X480LJ/X292.
11009 | This controller cannot load a program setting that uses a 21 megapixels or greater camera. | An attempt is being made to load a program setting that uses 21 megapixel or greater cameras into a controller that does not support 21 megapixel or greater cameras. | Load a program setting that uses a 21 megapixel or greater camera on the CV-X472/X482/X492/X292.
11011 | Failed to load because the resource memory of the program setting is beyond the size. | Resource memory is full in the program setting file loaded at startup. | • Switch to a different program setting file. • Correct the program setting such that it does not exceed the available resource memory.
 | | Resource memory is full in the program file loaded during program setting switching (or reloading). | • Switch to a different program setting file. • Correct the program setting such that it does not exceed the available resource memory.
11012 | This controller cannot load a program setting in which LumiTrax is enabled. | Attempted to load a program setting in which LumiTrax is enabled using the CV- X100/X300 Series. | Use the CV-X400/X200 Series if you want to enable LumiTrax.
11013 | Cannot load because LumiTrax is enabled in CA-HX500C/HX500M. | Attempted to load a program setting that uses CA-HX500C/HX500M with LumiTrax enabled using the CV-X272. | Use the CV-X292/X452/X472/X482/X492 to load a program setting that uses CA-HX500C/HX500M with LumiTrax enabled.

11014 | This controller cannot load a Vision-Guided Robotics setting. | An attempt is being made to load a program setting that uses Vision-Guided Robotics into a controller that does not support Vision-Guided Robotics. | Load the Vision-Guided Robotics setting with CV-X100/ X300 Series (F or A package) or CV-X400/X200 Series.
11015 | This controller cannot load a program setting where the Detection Target Selection Condition or Rotation Direction- Added Search is enabled in a Pattern Match (Profile) inspection or ShapeTrax3A. | Attempted to load a program setting where detection target selection conditions or rotation direction-added searches are enabled on ShapeTrax3A/ inspections using Pattern Match (Profile) on the CV-X100 Series. | If you want to enable detection target selection conditions or rotation direction-added searches on ShapeTrax3A/inspections using Pattern Match (Profile), use the CV-X400/X300 Series.

11017 | This controller cannot load a program setting where HDR capture is used with a CA-HX camera. | Attempted to load a program setting in which HDR capture is enabled on the CA-HX camera using the CV-X100 Series. | If you want to use program settings in which HDR capture is enabled on the CA-HX camera, use the CV- X400/X300 Series.
11018 | This controller cannot load a program setting where Flash 5 to 8 or the light controller 5 to 8 is used. | Attempted to load a program setting where Flash 5 to 8 or the light controller 5 to 8 is used using the CV-X100 Series. | If you want to use Flash 5 to 8 or Light Controller 5 to 8, use the CV-X400/X300 Series.

11020 | This controller cannot load a program setting where Gain has been changed in the Stain tool. | Attempted to load a program setting in which the gain was changed in the stain tool using the CV-X100 Series. | Load program settings in which the gain was changed in the stain tool using the CV-X400/X300 Series. Error Number: 10101; Error Messages: Light controller is disconnected. Verify the connection and power source of light controller.; Cause: Either the illumination expansion unit specified in the camera settings has been disconnected or the power is not turned on.; Remedy: Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is not damaged.
Error Number: 10102; Error Messages: The light controller has been reset because its initialization is detected.; Cause: The power to the connected illumination expansion unit has been cycled while the controller has remained on. Resulting in the resetting of the settings; Remedy: Check that the power supply to the illumination expansion unit is continuously stable. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly.
Error Number: 10103; Error Messages: An error occurred in the internal memory of the light controller*.; Cause: An error has occurred with the EEPROM data of the illumination expansion unit and the settings have been reset.; Remedy: • If using the DC illumination mode, perform linearization again and save the settings after restoring power. • If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
Error Number: 10104; Error Messages: Failed to initialize the light controller*.; Cause: Failed to perform initialization within the illumination expansion unit after starting up.; Remedy: If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.

Error Message: PCprogram communication has failed.; Cause: A communication error occurred in either the Ethernet or USB connection when outputting data to the PC program specified as the destination for a data output unit, image output unit, or as the output location for the image archive.; Corrective Action: • Make sure the Ethernet cable or USB cable is connected to the controller and the PC. • Make sure there are no problems (kinks, breaks etc) with the Ethernet or USB cable. • Check the Ethernet cable type (cross, straight). • Check whether the PC at the other end of the connection is ready to transmit/receive data. • Check that the correct PC program is running on the PC and that the PC is connected to the controller.; Error Code: 97
Error Message: PLC-Link communication has failed.; Cause: An error occurred in the connection with the PLC when the [PLC-Link (RS-232C)] or [PLC-Link (Ethernet)] function was enabled.; Corrective Action: • Check the connection with the PLC and the settings of the PLC. • If PLC link is not used, change communication mode to [Disable]. • If the error message displayed after a trigger input, check that the data memory destination specified is in the range that meets the PLC format.; Error Code: 112

Verify the connection and power source of light controller.; Cause: Either the illumination expansion unit specified in the camera settings has been disconnected or the power is not turned on.; Remedy: Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is not damaged.

top_results.title: AS_152507_CV-X_UM_C81US_KA_GB_2045_5.pdf
top_results.content:
Error Number: 10101; Error Messages: Light controller is disconnected. Verify the connection and power source of light controller.; Cause: Either the illumination expansion unit specified in the camera settings has been disconnected or the power is not turned on.; Remedy: Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is not damaged.
Error Number: 10102; Error Messages: The light controller has been reset because its initialization is detected.; Cause: The power to the connected illumination expansion unit has been cycled while the controller has remained on. Resulting in the resetting of the settings; Remedy: Check that the power supply to the illumination expansion unit is continuously stable. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly.
Error Number: 10103; Error Messages: An error occurred in the internal memory of the light controller*.; Cause: An error has occurred with the EEPROM data of the illumination expansion unit and the settings have been reset.; Remedy: • If using the DC illumination mode, perform linearization again and save the settings after restoring power. • If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
Error Number: 10104; Error Messages: Failed to initialize the light controller*.; Cause: Failed to perform initialization within the illumination expansion unit after starting up.; Remedy: If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.

9-94 CV-X UM_A

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
14128 | The following item does not match the Camera Settings. - LJ-V head luminance output type | The type of LJ-V Series heads specified in [Camera Settings] of the program is different from the type of LJ-V Series heads connected. | Check the model of the connected LJ-V Series heads.
14129 | The following item does not match the Camera Settings. - Number of LJ-V heads | The number of LJ-V Series heads specified in [Camera Settings] of the program is different from the number of LJ-V Series heads connected. | Check the number of connected LJ-V Series heads.
14130 | The following error occurred. - An unrecognizable LJ-V head is connected. | The connected LJ-V Series head does not support the controller. | Check the model of the connected LJ-V Series head.
14131 | The following error occurred. - The connected LJ-V head cannot be used in the CA- E100LJ. | An LJ-V Series head supporting luminance output is connected to CA- E100LJ. | Check the model of the connected LJ-V Series head.
14132 | The following error occurred. - There is no LJ-V head connected. | The LJ-V Series head is not connected to the camera input unit. | Check the connection between the camera input unit and the LJ-V Series head.
14133 | The following error occurred. - Please connect the LJ-V head to the Head A connector. | The LJ-V Series head is not connected to the head A connector. | Connect the LJ-V Series head to the head A connector.
14134 | The following error occurred. - Several differing LJ-V heads are connected. | Different LJ-V Series heads are connected to Head A and Head B. | Connect the same model of LJ-V Series head to Head A and Head B.
14135 | The following error occurred. - An abnormality occurred inside the LJ-V unit. | The LJ-V input unit is damaged. | Contact your local KEYENCE office.
14136 | The following error occurred. - An abnormality occurred inside the LJ-V head. | The LJ-V Series head is damaged. | Contact your local KEYENCE office.
14137 | The following error occurred. - The CA-E110LJ cannot be used on the CV-X480LJ. | CA-E110LJ is connected to the CV- X480LJ. | Check the connected camera input unit.

Error messages Troubleshooting

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
10101 | Light controller is disconnected. Verify the connection and power source of light controller. | Either the illumination expansion unit specified in the camera settings has been disconnected or the power is not turned on. | Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is not damaged.
10102 | The light controller has been reset because its initialization is detected. | The power to the connected illumination expansion unit has been cycled while the controller has remained on. Resulting in the resetting of the settings | Check that the power supply to the illumination expansion unit is continuously stable. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly.
10103 | An error occurred in the internal memory of the light controller*. | An error has occurred with the EEPROM data of the illumination expansion unit and the settings have been reset. | • If using the DC illumination mode, perform linearization again and save the settings after restoring power. • If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
10104 | Failed to initialize the light controller*. | Failed to perform initialization within the illumination expansion unit after starting up. | If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
10105 | Unrecognized external unit is connected. Confirm the external unit type after turning off the controller. | An external unit which is not supported by the controller is connected. | Confirm the model of the connected external unit.
10106 | The light is not connected. Check the connection of the light. | The light cannot be recognized. Or a communication error occurred between CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E and the light. | • Check that the CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E and the light are connected. • Check that the light cable is not broken or disconnected.
10107 | Overload state of Light Controller * - LIGHT ** was detected. Widen the lighting interval. | The light-on time of the light is too long when compared to the light-off time; therefore, the light is in the overloaded condition. | Adjust the trigger interval and/or shutter speed so the light-off time of the light becomes three times or more longer than the light-on time.
10108 | Cannot connect 3 or more CA- DC30E units. | Three or more CA-DC30E units are connected. | Only connect two or less CA-DC30E units to one controller.
10109 | An error occurred in the communication with the light controller (CA-DC60E/DC50E/ DC30E). Please adjust the flash output duration and timing. | The next FLASH was input while the light was being emitted (Communication with the controller cannot be established while the light emission is active). | • Set the FLASH output time to 0.1 msec (The lighting time of the light is linked with the camera shutter speed). However, the maximum lighting time is 100 msec). • Set the period from capture start to flash output closer to zero. • If the error persists even after adjusting the FLASH output time and the FLASH timing, increase the trigger interval.
10110 | The light controller is one that does not support the LumiTrax function. | The light selected as the LumiTrax light is connected to a light controller other than CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E. | Check that the light selected as the LumiTrax light is connected to CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E.
10111 | The light controller is one that does not support HDR. | It was detected that the light assigned to the camera where HDR is enabled is connected to CA-DC50E/DC30E. | Assign a light that is connected to a light controller other than the CA-DC50E/DC30E for the light to use for the HDR.
10112 | The model of light controller that is set in the Light Controller Settings is not connected. | The connected light controller does not match the light controller type specified in the light controller model selection setting in [Camera Settings]. | Check the model of the connected light controller and the setting content.
 | | A non-connected light controller is specified in the light controller model selection setting in [Camera Settings]. | Turn off the controller and connect the specified light controller.
10113 | Overcurrent was detected in the connected light. Please check the connected light and power up again. | Excessive current flowed through the light controller. | If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
10115 | Continuous lighting cannot be used because Volume Limit is disabled. | The volume limit for the light unit where Continuous is set as the emission timing is disabled. | • Enable the volume limit. • Set emission timing to a setting other than continuous lighting.
10116 | The internal temperature of light head ** is high. (Light Controller *) As this may cause a breakdown, please check the installation condition and ambient temperature. | The temperature rating was exceeded due to heat generation caused by overload on the light. Or the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value. | • Check the light volume, shutter speed and emission timing, and reduce the load on the light. • Check if the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value.
10117 | The light head has been reset because its initialization was detected. | As the settings written to the light head were reset when the light head that could not be recognized was recognized again, the settings were written again. | Check that power is being supplied continuously to the light head and that it is connected correctly.
10120 | The light head is still warming up internally. It takes about * minutes after the error message was displayed for the warm-up to be finished. | The light head is warming up to ensure stable operation. | • Wait until the warm-up finishes with the power switched ON. • It is possible to use the unit while it is warming up, but you are advised to wait until the warm-up completion for stable operation. • The displayed warm-up completion time is only an estimate as it depends on the outside temperature and the temperature of the light head.
10121 | The system was stopped because the internal temperature of light head ** has exceeded the prescribed value. (Light Controller *) Please turn off the power temporarily and check the installation condition and ambient temperature. | The temperature rating was exceeded due to heat generation caused by overload on the light. Or the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value. | • Check the light volume, shutter speed and emission timing, and reduce the load on the light. • Check if the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value.
10122 | The system was stopped because a malfunction in the internal device of Light Controller *'s light head ** was detected. | The internal state of the light head is abnormal. | Contact the nearest KEYENCE office.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
10126 | This controller cannot load a program setting where Outline Capture is used. | The user attempted to load a program that uses Outline Capture Mode on the CV-X300 Series. | Use the CV-X400 Series if you wish to use Outline Capture Mode.
10127 | This controller cannot load a program setting where 3D Capture is used. | The user attempted to load a program that uses 3D Capture Mode on the CV- X300 Series. | Use the CV-X400 Series if you wish to use 3D Capture Mode.
11001 | Unable to load the selected program setting file. | The program file that corresponds to the last saved program No. (or the program No. selected using the mouse) does not exist. | Change the program number to a working program.
 | | The program file for the specified program could not be found when changing or reloading programs. | Change the program number to a working program.
11002 | Failed to load because the image memory of the program setting is beyond the size. | The image memory for the program file loaded at startup is full. | • Change to a different program file. • Correct the program to reduce the size of its data.
 | | The program being loaded exceeds the available image memory. | • Change to a different program file. • Correct the program to reduce the size of its data.
11003 | Failed to load the system setting. | The system settings file used at startup cannot be found on SD Card 1. | Before powering up the controller, make sure the system settings file exists on the SD card.
 | | The system settings loaded at startup is from a incompatible version. | Create a compatible version of the system settings file.
 | | The system settings file has a checksum error. | Use a different system settings file.
 | | The system settings file loaded at startup is damaged. | Use a different system settings file.
11004 | Unable to load the program setting file due to unsupported version. | The program loaded at startup is an incompatible version. | Change the program to a different working program.
 | | The program being loaded is an incompatible version. | Create a compatible version of the program file.
11005 | Unable to load the program setting file due to checksum errors. | The program loaded at startup has a checksum error. | Change the program to a different working program.
 | | The program being loaded has a checksum error. | Recreate the program file.
11006 | Unable to load the program setting file due to damage. | The program loaded at startup is damaged. | Change the program to a different working program.
 | | The program being loaded is damaged. | Recreate the program file.
11007 | This controller cannot load program setting (connector). | A connector-dedicated program setting is being loaded to a controller that does not support connector inspection. | Load the connector-dedicated program setting on the CV-X4*2F, CV-X3*2F, CV-X3*2M, CV-X2*2F, CV-X1*2F or CV-X1*2M.
11008 | This controller cannot load a program setting that uses an LJ-V. | An attempt is being made to load a program setting that uses the LJ-V Series head into a controller that does not support the LJ-V Series head. | Load a program setting that uses the LJ-V Series head on the CV-X482/X480LJ/X292.
11009 | This controller cannot load a program setting that uses a 21 megapixels or greater camera. | An attempt is being made to load a program setting that uses 21 megapixel or greater cameras into a controller that does not support 21 megapixel or greater cameras. | Load a program setting that uses a 21 megapixel or greater camera on the CV-X472/X482/X492/X292.
11011 | Failed to load because the resource memory of the program setting is beyond the size. | Resource memory is full in the program setting file loaded at startup. | • Switch to a different program setting file. • Correct the program setting such that it does not exceed the available resource memory.
 | | Resource memory is full in the program file loaded during program setting switching (or reloading). | • Switch to a different program setting file. • Correct the program setting such that it does not exceed the available resource memory.
11012 | This controller cannot load a program setting in which LumiTrax is enabled. | Attempted to load a program setting in which LumiTrax is enabled using the CV- X100/X300 Series. | Use the CV-X400/X200 Series if you want to enable LumiTrax.
11013 | Cannot load because LumiTrax is enabled in CA-HX500C/HX500M. | Attempted to load a program setting that uses CA-HX500C/HX500M with LumiTrax enabled using the CV-X272. | Use the CV-X292/X452/X472/X482/X492 to load a program setting that uses CA-HX500C/HX500M with LumiTrax enabled.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
11014 | This controller cannot load a Vision-Guided Robotics setting. | An attempt is being made to load a program setting that uses Vision-Guided Robotics into a controller that does not support Vision-Guided Robotics. | Load the Vision-Guided Robotics setting with CV-X100/ X300 Series (F or A package) or CV-X400/X200 Series.
11015 | This controller cannot load a program setting where the Detection Target Selection Condition or Rotation Direction- Added Search is enabled in a Pattern Match (Profile) inspection or ShapeTrax3A. | Attempted to load a program setting where detection target selection conditions or rotation direction-added searches are enabled on ShapeTrax3A/ inspections using Pattern Match (Profile) on the CV-X100 Series. | If you want to enable detection target selection conditions or rotation direction-added searches on ShapeTrax3A/inspections using Pattern Match (Profile), use the CV-X400/X300 Series.
11016 | This controller cannot load a program setting that uses a USB HDD. | Attempted to load a program setting where USB HDD is used using the CV- X100 Series. | If you want to use the USB HDD, use the CV-X400/X300 Series.
11017 | This controller cannot load a program setting where HDR capture is used with a CA-HX camera. | Attempted to load a program setting in which HDR capture is enabled on the CA-HX camera using the CV-X100 Series. | If you want to use program settings in which HDR capture is enabled on the CA-HX camera, use the CV- X400/X300 Series.
11018 | This controller cannot load a program setting where Flash 5 to 8 or the light controller 5 to 8 is used. | Attempted to load a program setting where Flash 5 to 8 or the light controller 5 to 8 is used using the CV-X100 Series. | If you want to use Flash 5 to 8 or Light Controller 5 to 8, use the CV-X400/X300 Series.
11019 | This controller cannot load a program setting where MultiSpectrum is used. | Attempted to load a program setting where MultiSpectrum Mode is used using the CV-X100/X300 Series. | If you want to use MultiSpectrum mode, use the CV- X400 Series.
11020 | This controller cannot load a program setting where Gain has been changed in the Stain tool. | Attempted to load a program setting in which the gain was changed in the stain tool using the CV-X100 Series. | Load program settings in which the gain was changed in the stain tool using the CV-X400/X300 Series. Alternatively, set the stain tool gain to 1.0 with the CV- X400/X300 Series before loading the program setting on the CV-X100 Series.
11028 | Cannot load because LumiTrax is enabled in a 21 megapixels or greater camera. | An attempt is being made to load a program setting that uses LumiTrax Mode with a 21 megapixel or greater camera into a controller that does not support the LumiTrax Mode used by a 21 megapixel or greater camera. | Load a program setting that uses LumiTrax Mode with a 21 megapixel or greater mode camera onto the CV-X492.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
12001 | Failed to access SD Card 1. | A problem occurred while trying to access SD Card 1. SD Card 1 could be faulty. | • From the [Manage Files] menu, run the [Check] utility on SD Card 1. • If the error persists, format the SD Card. (Note, this will erase all contents on SD Card 1.) • If the problem cannot be resolved by any of these remedies, the SD card may be damaged.
 | | The controller could not recognize the format of SD Card 1. | • From the [Manage Files] menu, run the [Check] utility on SD Card 1. • If the error persists, format the SD Card.  | | An unsupported SD card is being used. | The functionality and performance when using commercially available (non-industrial rated) SD cards is not guaranteed
 | | The destination file is set to read-only. | Disable the read-only setting on the destination file, or delete it.
12002 | Failed to access SD Card 2. | A problem occurred while trying to access SD Card 2. | • From the [Manage Files] menu, run the [Check] utility on SD Card 2. • If the error persists, format the SD Card. (Note, this will erase all contents on SD Card 2.) • If the problem cannot be resolved by any of these remedies, the SD card may be damaged.
 | | The controller could not recognize the format of SD Card 2. | • From the [Manage Files] menu, run the [Check] utility on SD Card 2. • If the error persists, format the SD Card. (Note, this will erase all contents on SD Card 2.) • If the problem cannot be resolved by any of these remedies, the SD card may be damaged.
 | | An unsupported SD card is being used. | The functionality and performance when using commercially available (non-industrial rated) SD cards is not guaranteed
 | | The destination file is set to read-only. | Disable the read-only setting on the destination file, or delete it.
 | | A large number of files was output to one folder. | There is a limit to the number of files that can be output to one folder and this error occurs when this limit is reached. Do not output a large number of files to one folder.
12003 | SD Card 1 is full. | There is not enough free space on SD Card 1. | Make space available by deleting or moving unnecessary files.
12004 | SD Card 2 is full. | There is not enough free space on SD Card 2. | Make space available by deleting or moving unnecessary files.
12005 | Insert SD Card 1. | No SD card in SD1 slot. An unsupported SD card is being used. | Properly insert an SD card into the SD1 slot. The functionality and performance when using commercially available (non-industrial rated) SD cards is not guaranteed
12006 | Insert SD Card 2. | No SD card in SD2 slot. After executing [Remove SD Card2], no SD card has been reinserted into SD2 slot. | Properly insert an SD card into the SD2 slot. If the SD card is already inserted, remove it first, and then insert it again. The functionality and performance when using
 | | An unsupported SD card is being used. | commercially available (non-industrial rated) SD cards is not guaranteed
12007 | Cannot find SD Card 1. Be sure to keep the SD card 1 inserted during the power on. | SD Card 1 was removed while the power was ON. | Do not remove SD Card 1 while the power is ON. Removing an SD card while it is being accessed may damage the SD card and the data saved on it.
12008 | Execute the eject operation before removing the SD Card 2. The SD card and files may be damaged. | The SD Card 2 was removed without using the [Remove SD Card2] function. | Use the [Remove SD Card2] function to safely remove SD Card 2. Error Number: 10101; Error Messages: Light controller is disconnected. Verify the connection and power source of light controller.; Cause: Either the illumination expansion unit specified in the camera settings has been disconnected or the power is not turned on.; Remedy: Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is not damaged.
Error Number: 10102; Error Messages: The light controller has been reset because its initialization is detected.; Cause: The power to the connected illumination expansion unit has been cycled while the controller has remained on. Resulting in the resetting of the settings; Remedy: Check that the power supply to the illumination expansion unit is continuously stable. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly.
Error Number: 10103; Error Messages: An error occurred in the internal memory of the light controller*.; Cause: An error has occurred with the EEPROM data of the illumination expansion unit and the settings have been reset.; Remedy: • If using the DC illumination mode, perform linearization again and save the settings after restoring power. • If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
Error Number: 10104; Error Messages: Failed to initialize the light controller*.; Cause: Failed to perform initialization within the illumination expansion unit after starting up.; Remedy: If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.

Error Number: 10126; Error Messages: This controller cannot load a program setting where Outline Capture is used.; Cause: The user attempted to load a program that uses Outline Capture Mode on the CV-X300 Series.; Remedy: Use the CV-X400 Series if you wish to use Outline Capture Mode.
Error Number: 10127; Error Messages: This controller cannot load a program setting where 3D Capture is used.; Cause: The user attempted to load a program that uses 3D Capture Mode on the CV- X300 Series.; Remedy: Use the CV-X400 Series if you wish to use 3D Capture Mode.
Error Number: 11001; Error Messages: Unable to load the selected program setting file.; Cause: The program file that corresponds to the last saved program No. (or the program No. selected using the mouse) does not exist.; Remedy: Change the program number to a working program.
The program file for the specified program could not be found when changing or reloading programs. | Change the program number to a working program.

AS_152507_CV-X_UM_C81US_KA_GB_2045_5.pdf | 9-94 CV-X UM_A

Error messages Troubleshooting

AS_152507_CV-X_UM_C81US_KA_GB_2045_5.pdf | 9-94 CV-X UM_A

9-94 CV-X UM_A

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
14128 | The following item does not match the Camera Settings. - LJ-V head luminance output type | The type of LJ-V Series heads specified in [Camera Settings] of the program is different from the type of LJ-V Series heads connected. | Check the model of the connected LJ-V Series heads.
14129 | The following item does not match the Camera Settings. - Number of LJ-V heads | The number of LJ-V Series heads specified in [Camera Settings] of the program is different from the number of LJ-V Series heads connected. | Check the number of connected LJ-V Series heads.
14130 | The following error occurred. - An unrecognizable LJ-V head is connected. | The connected LJ-V Series head does not support the controller. | Check the model of the connected LJ-V Series head.
14131 | The following error occurred. - The connected LJ-V head cannot be used in the CA- E100LJ. | An LJ-V Series head supporting luminance output is connected to CA- E100LJ. | Check the model of the connected LJ-V Series head.
14132 | The following error occurred. - There is no LJ-V head connected. | The LJ-V Series head is not connected to the camera input unit. | Check the connection between the camera input unit and the LJ-V Series head.
14133 | The following error occurred. - Please connect the LJ-V head to the Head A connector. | The LJ-V Series head is not connected to the head A connector. | Connect the LJ-V Series head to the head A connector.
14134 | The following error occurred. - Several differing LJ-V heads are connected. | Different LJ-V Series heads are connected to Head A and Head B. | Connect the same model of LJ-V Series head to Head A and Head B.
14135 | The following error occurred. - An abnormality occurred inside the LJ-V unit. | The LJ-V input unit is damaged. | Contact your local KEYENCE office.
14136 | The following error occurred. - An abnormality occurred inside the LJ-V head. | The LJ-V Series head is damaged. | Contact your local KEYENCE office.
14137 | The following error occurred. - The CA-E110LJ cannot be used on the CV-X480LJ. | CA-E110LJ is connected to the CV- X480LJ. | Check the connected camera input unit.

Error messages Troubleshooting

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
10101 | Light controller is disconnected. Verify the connection and power source of light controller. | Either the illumination expansion unit specified in the camera settings has been disconnected or the power is not turned on. | Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is not damaged.
10102 | The light controller has been reset because its initialization is detected. | The power to the connected illumination expansion unit has been cycled while the controller has remained on. Resulting in the resetting of the settings | Check that the power supply to the illumination expansion unit is continuously stable. Make sure the illumination expansion unit is attached correctly.
10103 | An error occurred in the internal memory of the light controller*. | An error has occurred with the EEPROM data of the illumination expansion unit and the settings have been reset. | • If using the DC illumination mode, perform linearization again and save the settings after restoring power. • If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
10104 | Failed to initialize the light controller*. | Failed to perform initialization within the illumination expansion unit after starting up. | If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the illumination expansion unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.
10105 | Unrecognized external unit is connected. Confirm the external unit type after turning off the controller. | An external unit which is not supported by the controller is connected. | Confirm the model of the connected external unit.
10106 | The light is not connected. Check the connection of the light. | The light cannot be recognized. Or a communication error occurred between CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E and the light. | • Check that the CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E and the light are connected. • Check that the light cable is not broken or disconnected.
10107 | Overload state of Light Controller * - LIGHT ** was detected. Widen the lighting interval. | The light-on time of the light is too long when compared to the light-off time; therefore, the light is in the overloaded condition. | Adjust the trigger interval and/or shutter speed so the light-off time of the light becomes three times or more longer than the light-on time.
10108 | Cannot connect 3 or more CA- DC30E units. | Three or more CA-DC30E units are connected. | Only connect two or less CA-DC30E units to one controller.
10109 | An error occurred in the communication with the light controller (CA-DC60E/DC50E/ DC30E). Please adjust the flash output duration and timing. | The next FLASH was input while the light was being emitted (Communication with the controller cannot be established while the light emission is active). | • Set the FLASH output time to 0.1 msec (The lighting time of the light is linked with the camera shutter speed). However, the maximum lighting time is 100 msec). • Set the period from capture start to flash output closer to zero. • If the error persists even after adjusting the FLASH output time and the FLASH timing, increase the trigger interval.
10110 | The light controller is one that does not support the LumiTrax function. | The light selected as the LumiTrax light is connected to a light controller other than CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E. | Check that the light selected as the LumiTrax light is connected to CA-DC60E/DC50E/DC30E.
10111 | The light controller is one that does not support HDR. | It was detected that the light assigned to the camera where HDR is enabled is connected to CA-DC50E/DC30E. | Assign a light that is connected to a light controller other than the CA-DC50E/DC30E for the light to use for the HDR.
10112 | The model of light controller that is set in the Light Controller Settings is not connected. | The connected light controller does not match the light controller type specified in the light controller model selection setting in [Camera Settings]. | Check the model of the connected light controller and the setting content.
 | | A non-connected light controller is specified in the light controller model selection setting in [Camera Settings]. | Turn off the controller and connect the specified light controller.
10113 | Overcurrent was detected in the connected light. Please check the connected light and power up again. | Excessive current flowed through the light controller. | If errors continue to occur after restoring power, the unit may be damaged. Contact your local KEYENCE office.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
10115 | Continuous lighting cannot be used because Volume Limit is disabled. | The volume limit for the light unit where Continuous is set as the emission timing is disabled. | • Enable the volume limit. • Set emission timing to a setting other than continuous lighting.
10116 | The internal temperature of light head ** is high. (Light Controller *) As this may cause a breakdown, please check the installation condition and ambient temperature. | The temperature rating was exceeded due to heat generation caused by overload on the light. Or the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value. | • Check the light volume, shutter speed and emission timing, and reduce the load on the light. • Check if the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value.
10117 | The light head has been reset because its initialization was detected. | As the settings written to the light head were reset when the light head that could not be recognized was recognized again, the settings were written again. | Check that power is being supplied continuously to the light head and that it is connected correctly.
10120 | The light head is still warming up internally. It takes about * minutes after the error message was displayed for the warm-up to be finished. | The light head is warming up to ensure stable operation. | • Wait until the warm-up finishes with the power switched ON. • It is possible to use the unit while it is warming up, but you are advised to wait until the warm-up completion for stable operation. • The displayed warm-up completion time is only an estimate as it depends on the outside temperature and the temperature of the light head.
10121 | The system was stopped because the internal temperature of light head ** has exceeded the prescribed value. (Light Controller *) Please turn off the power temporarily and check the installation condition and ambient temperature. | The temperature rating was exceeded due to heat generation caused by overload on the light. Or the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value. | • Check the light volume, shutter speed and emission timing, and reduce the load on the light. • Check if the ambient temperature exceeds the rated value.
10122 | The system was stopped because a malfunction in the internal device of Light Controller *'s light head ** was detected. | The internal state of the light head is abnormal. | Contact the nearest KEYENCE office.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
10126 | This controller cannot load a program setting where Outline Capture is used. | The user attempted to load a program that uses Outline Capture Mode on the CV-X300 Series. | Use the CV-X400 Series if you wish to use Outline Capture Mode.
10127 | This controller cannot load a program setting where 3D Capture is used. | The user attempted to load a program that uses 3D Capture Mode on the CV- X300 Series. | Use the CV-X400 Series if you wish to use 3D Capture Mode.
11001 | Unable to load the selected program setting file. | The program file that corresponds to the last saved program No. (or the program No. selected using the mouse) does not exist. | Change the program number to a working program.
 | | The program file for the specified program could not be found when changing or reloading programs. | Change the program number to a working program.
11002 | Failed to load because the image memory of the program setting is beyond the size. | The image memory for the program file loaded at startup is full. | • Change to a different program file. • Correct the program to reduce the size of its data.
 | | The program being loaded exceeds the available image memory. | • Change to a different program file. • Correct the program to reduce the size of its data.
11003 | Failed to load the system setting. | The system settings file used at startup cannot be found on SD Card 1. | Before powering up the controller, make sure the system settings file exists on the SD card.
 | | The system settings loaded at startup is from a incompatible version. | Create a compatible version of the system settings file.
 | | The system settings file has a checksum error. | Use a different system settings file.
 | | The system settings file loaded at startup is damaged. | Use a different system settings file.
11004 | Unable to load the program setting file due to unsupported version. | The program loaded at startup is an incompatible version. | Change the program to a different working program.
 | | The program being loaded is an incompatible version. | Create a compatible version of the program file.
11005 | Unable to load the program setting file due to checksum errors. | The program loaded at startup has a checksum error. | Change the program to a different working program.
 | | The program being loaded has a checksum error. | Recreate the program file.
11006 | Unable to load the program setting file due to damage. | The program loaded at startup is damaged. | Change the program to a different working program.
 | | The program being loaded is damaged. | Recreate the program file.
11007 | This controller cannot load program setting (connector). | A connector-dedicated program setting is being loaded to a controller that does not support connector inspection. | Load the connector-dedicated program setting on the CV-X4*2F, CV-X3*2F, CV-X3*2M, CV-X2*2F, CV-X1*2F or CV-X1*2M.
11008 | This controller cannot load a program setting that uses an LJ-V. | An attempt is being made to load a program setting that uses the LJ-V Series head into a controller that does not support the LJ-V Series head. | Load a program setting that uses the LJ-V Series head on the CV-X482/X480LJ/X292.
11009 | This controller cannot load a program setting that uses a 21 megapixels or greater camera. | An attempt is being made to load a program setting that uses 21 megapixel or greater cameras into a controller that does not support 21 megapixel or greater cameras. | Load a program setting that uses a 21 megapixel or greater camera on the CV-X472/X482/X492/X292.
11011 | Failed to load because the resource memory of the program setting is beyond the size. | Resource memory is full in the program setting file loaded at startup. | • Switch to a different program setting file. • Correct the program setting such that it does not exceed the available resource memory.
 | | Resource memory is full in the program file loaded during program setting switching (or reloading). | • Switch to a different program setting file. • Correct the program setting such that it does not exceed the available resource memory.
11012 | This controller cannot load a program setting in which LumiTrax is enabled. | Attempted to load a program setting in which LumiTrax is enabled using the CV- X100/X300 Series. | Use the CV-X400/X200 Series if you want to enable LumiTrax.
11013 | Cannot load because LumiTrax is enabled in CA-HX500C/HX500M. | Attempted to load a program setting that uses CA-HX500C/HX500M with LumiTrax enabled using the CV-X272. | Use the CV-X292/X452/X472/X482/X492 to load a program setting that uses CA-HX500C/HX500M with LumiTrax enabled.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
11014 | This controller cannot load a Vision-Guided Robotics setting. | An attempt is being made to load a program setting that uses Vision-Guided Robotics into a controller that does not support Vision-Guided Robotics. | Load the Vision-Guided Robotics setting with CV-X100/ X300 Series (F or A package) or CV-X400/X200 Series.
11015 | This controller cannot load a program setting where the Detection Target Selection Condition or Rotation Direction- Added Search is enabled in a Pattern Match (Profile) inspection or ShapeTrax3A. | Attempted to load a program setting where detection target selection conditions or rotation direction-added searches are enabled on ShapeTrax3A/ inspections using Pattern Match (Profile) on the CV-X100 Series. | If you want to enable detection target selection conditions or rotation direction-added searches on ShapeTrax3A/inspections using Pattern Match (Profile), use the CV-X400/X300 Series.
11016 | This controller cannot load a program setting that uses a USB HDD. | Attempted to load a program setting where USB HDD is used using the CV- X100 Series. | If you want to use the USB HDD, use the CV-X400/X300 Series.
11017 | This controller cannot load a program setting where HDR capture is used with a CA-HX camera. | Attempted to load a program setting in which HDR capture is enabled on the CA-HX camera using the CV-X100 Series. | If you want to use program settings in which HDR capture is enabled on the CA-HX camera, use the CV- X400/X300 Series.
11018 | This controller cannot load a program setting where Flash 5 to 8 or the light controller 5 to 8 is used. | Attempted to load a program setting where Flash 5 to 8 or the light controller 5 to 8 is used using the CV-X100 Series. | If you want to use Flash 5 to 8 or Light Controller 5 to 8, use the CV-X400/X300 Series.
11019 | This controller cannot load a program setting where MultiSpectrum is used. | Attempted to load a program setting where MultiSpectrum Mode is used using the CV-X100/X300 Series. | If you want to use MultiSpectrum mode, use the CV- X400 Series.
11020 | This controller cannot load a program setting where Gain has been changed in the Stain tool. | Attempted to load a program setting in which the gain was changed in the stain tool using the CV-X100 Series. | Load program settings in which the gain was changed in the stain tool using the CV-X400/X300 Series. Alternatively, set the stain tool gain to 1.0 with the CV- X400/X300 Series before loading the program setting on the CV-X100 Series.
11028 | Cannot load because LumiTrax is enabled in a 21 megapixels or greater camera. | An attempt is being made to load a program setting that uses LumiTrax Mode with a 21 megapixel or greater camera into a controller that does not support the LumiTrax Mode used by a 21 megapixel or greater camera. | Load a program setting that uses LumiTrax Mode with a 21 megapixel or greater mode camera onto the CV-X492.

Error Number | Error Messages | Cause | Remedy
12001 | Failed to access SD Card 1. | A problem occurred while trying to access SD Card 1. SD Card 1 could be faulty. | • From the [Manage Files] menu, run the [Check] utility on SD Card 1. • If the error persists, format the SD Card. (Note, this will erase all contents on SD Card 1.) • If the problem cannot be resolved by any of these remedies, the SD card may be damaged.
 | | The controller could not recognize the format of SD Card 1. | • From the [Manage Files] menu, run the [Check] utility on SD Card 1. • If the error persists, format the SD Card. (Note, this will erase all contents on SD Card 1.) • If the problem cannot be resolved by any of these remedies, the SD card may be damaged.
 | | An unsupported SD card is being used. | The functionality and performance when using commercially available (non-industrial rated) SD cards is not guaranteed
 | | The destination file is set to read-only. | Disable the read-only setting on the destination file, or delete it.
12002 | Failed to access SD Card 2. | A problem occurred while trying to access SD Card 2. | • From the [Manage Files] menu, run the [Check] utility on SD Card 2. • If the error persists, format the SD Card. (Note, this will erase all contents on SD Card 2.) • If the problem cannot be resolved by any of these remedies, the SD card may be damaged.
 | | The controller could not recognize the format of SD Card 2. | • From the [Manage Files] menu, run the [Check] utility on SD Card 2. • If the error persists, format the SD Card. (Note, this will erase all contents on SD Card 2.) • If the problem cannot be resolved by any of these remedies, the SD card may be damaged.
 | | An unsupported SD card is being used. | The functionality and performance when using commercially available (non-industrial rated) SD cards is not guaranteed
 | | The destination file is set to read-only. | Disable the read-only setting on the destination file, or delete it.
 | | A large number of files was output to one folder. | There is a limit to the number of files that can be output to one folder and this error occurs when this limit is reached. Do not output a large number of files to one folder.
12003 | SD Card 1 is full. | There is not enough free space on SD Card 1. | Make space available by deleting or moving unnecessary files.
12004 | SD Card 2 is full. | There is not enough free space on SD Card 2. | Make space available by deleting or moving unnecessary files.
12005 | Insert SD Card 1. | No SD card in SD1 slot. An unsupported SD card is being used. | Properly insert an SD card into the SD1 slot. The functionality and performance when using commercially available (non-industrial rated) SD cards is not guaranteed
12006 | Insert SD Card 2. | No SD card in SD2 slot. After executing [Remove SD Card2], no SD card has been reinserted into SD2 slot. | Properly insert an SD card into the SD2 slot. If the SD card is already inserted, remove it first, and then insert it again. The functionality and performance when using
 | | An unsupported SD card is being used. | commercially available (non-industrial rated) SD cards is not guaranteed
12007 | Cannot find SD Card 1. Be sure to keep the SD card 1 inserted during the power on. | SD Card 1 was removed while the power was ON. | Do not remove SD Card 1 while the power is ON. Removing an SD card while it is being accessed may damage the SD card and the data saved on it.
12008 | Execute the eject operation before removing the SD Card 2. The SD card and files may be damaged. | The SD Card 2 was removed without using the [Remove SD Card2] function. | Use the [Remove SD Card2] function to safely remove SD Card 2. Removing an SD card while it is being accessed may damage the SD card and the data saved on it.
